clue.text: Present final Loose Women on time

parts.note: a final is an end

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters of the next word are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A daytime TV chat show's last episode running to schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose Women is a British daytime TV chat show, so 'Loose' looks like part of a title; it is the anagram signal, turning WOMEN into OWMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A present, as a noun, is a gift, and an endowment is a gift of money or property.

clue.text: Even outsiders love restitched sports coat

indicators.note: outsiders says take the outer letters of the word even
restitched says the letters are sewn back together in a new order

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school sports

explanation.surface: A tailor has resewn a sports jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports coat' looks like one item, but 'sports' gives PE and 'coat' is the definition; 'restitched' turns LOVE into VELO.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is an enclosing cover or layer, as a coat is a covering layer.

clue.text: Material that's dug up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: dug, as from a mine, means mined

explanation.surface: A fabric excavated from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton fabric, a type of material.

clue.text: Absurdly, I study a Welsh flag outside English ground

indicators.note: outside says the Welsh flag letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: a flag is an emblem

indicators.note: absurdly says the letters are jumbled into a nonsensical order

explanation.surface: Someone studies a Welsh flag at an English sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurdly' jumbles I, the word study and A; 'outside' wraps the flag letters around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley Stadium in London is the English national football ground.

clue.text: Constituent ingredient of carrot/celery turnover!

indicators.note: turnover says the hidden letters are read backwards
an ingredient is one part of a mixture, so the answer is a part inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A vegetable pastry, a turnover made of carrot and celery.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Constituent ingredient' as the definition, but 'ingredient of' signals the hidden letters and only 'Constituent' defines the answer. A turnover is also a filled pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a voter in an electoral district, someone entitled to choose a representative.

clue.text: Accountant follows people to see part of New York

indicators.note: follows says the accountant comes after the people

parts.note: a tribe is a people
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant tags along behind a crowd to visit Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: Tribeca, the Triangle Below Canal Street, is a Lower Manhattan neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribeca is a district of Lower Manhattan, so a part of New York.

clue.text: Regularly read soldier's poems

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the word soldier's

explanation.surface: A soldier's verses are read aloud at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, often addressed to a person or thing.

clue.text: Ten events the old can fancy

indicators.note: fancy in its sense of elaborate or ornate says the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Older people may enjoy a ten-part contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics competition made up of ten separate track and field disciplines.

clue.text: Persuade escort to entertain foreign nobleman

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to see someone home is to escort them
duc is French for a duke

explanation.surface: Coaxing a companion to host a visiting aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to lure or entice someone, a strong kind of persuasion.

clue.text: Removing stimulant affected gin in a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says the gin in a cocktail ruined the coffee-free drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a cocktail' looks like where the gin is, but 'in' and 'a' are fodder too, beside AFFECTED and GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is a stimulant, and taking it out of coffee or tea is decaffeinating.

clue.text: VE Day overturned bitterness

indicators.note: overturned says the day's letters are flipped round

parts.note: MON is the short form of Monday, a day

explanation.surface: Victory in Europe Day is reversed, leaving resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: VE is taken as written; 'overturned' turns MON into NOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in its figurative sense is spite or bitter ill will.

clue.text: Offered as proof it's not all bad: actress takes journalist for husband

indicators.note: not all says the last letter of the word for bad is dropped

parts.note: bad means evil

indicators.note: takes one thing for another says a letter is swapped out and replaced
for completes takes X for Y: X stands where Y stood before

parts.note: Judi Dench is a famous British actress
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband
ED, an editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A defence of an actress whose husband is swapped for a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' trims EVIL to EVI; 'takes ... for' puts ED in place of the H of DENCH, giving DENCED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have evidenced something is to have shown or presented it as supporting proof.

clue.text: Illuminated a politician's home in the register that's been flipped

indicators.note: being home in something means sitting inside it
flipped says the word for the register is turned back to front

parts.note: a till is a cash register
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician's house lit up and listed on an upside-down register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been flipped' reverses the register word; 'home in' puts A and the politician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lamplit is lit by a lamp, so it is illuminated.

clue.text: Supple Italian wine first to cork after the Spanish

indicators.note: after says the wine and cork letter follow the Spanish article

parts.note: EL is 'the' in Spanish
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont

indicators.note: first to says take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Uncorking an Italian wine after the Spanish one.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and elastic both describe something flexible that bends and springs back.

clue.text: Sensational story that's p-petrifying

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
petrifying means dreadful

explanation.surface: A scary tale, told with a frightened stutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'p-' looks like fear, but it is a separate piece: p for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny dreadfuls were cheap lurid Victorian serial thrillers, sensational stories sold for a penny.

clue.text: Bizarrely, "our big hen" is how Sunak might describe Johnson

indicators.note: bizarrely says the letters are made strange by being jumbled

explanation.surface: A strange remark about a large chicken as a political put-down.
explanation.walkthrough: As Chancellor, Rishi Sunak lived at 11 Downing Street, next door to Prime Minister Boris Johnson at Number 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunak and Johnson lived in adjoining Downing Street houses, so each lived next door to the other.

clue.text: Weather-wise, an incoming cold front would make it exciting

indicators.note: incoming says the letter arrives inside the word to make it
would make it says adding the letter to the answer gives the exciting word, so here it is taken away

parts.note: exciting, building to a climax, means climactic

indicators.note: front says take the first letter of the word cold

explanation.surface: A weather report: an approaching cold front would liven things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The cold front sounds like meteorology, but it is just C: put C inside the answer and it becomes CLIMACTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic means relating to climate, the long-term pattern of weather.

clue.text: I directed online rant at footballer?

indicators.note: directed suggests the letters are arranged, as a director arranges things

explanation.surface: Someone sends an online tirade at a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directed' looks like aiming the rant, but signals rearranging ONLINE, RANT and AT, after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer capped for their country is called an international; the question mark admits this is only one kind.

clue.text: She's pragmatic about a catalogue

definitions.note: a whole statement describing a person, matched by the noun for such a person

parts.note: RE means about, as in a letter heading
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A sensible woman's view of a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a person who is practical and down-to-earth, facing facts rather than ideals.

clue.text: Part of London one learns about

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: about here means around, so the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A newcomer learns about a district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is an area of north London named after its tube station and football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a district of north London around the Emirates Stadium, with its own Underground station.

clue.text: Falling star to encounter gloomy fellow on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio says the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to encounter is to meet, and Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A shooting star and a meeting with a depressed man, heard on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling or shooting star is the popular name for a streak of light from a space rock burning up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Initially excited conservationist has isolated genetic code for odd beast

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letters of the four words that follow

parts.note: DNA carries the genetic code

explanation.surface: A thrilled conservationist has sequenced the DNA of a strange creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea, is a famously peculiar animal.

clue.text: Celebrity starts to stupidly tell Doctor Doctor gag, essentially, backwards

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the next two words
backwards says the doctors and the heart of the gag are read in reverse together

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: essentially says take the central letter, the essence of the word

explanation.surface: Fame comes from telling a silly 'Doctor, Doctor' joke the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor, Doctor' jokes are a classic British joke format. 'backwards' turns MO + DR + A into ARDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being famous, which is celebrity in its abstract sense.

clue.text: Start eating most of finger, top of nail

indicators.note: most of says the last letter of the finger word is dropped

parts.note: a digit is a finger

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Nibbling a fingernail.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is an idiom for starting to eat heartily.

clue.text: You must polish, not oil, cue… it's what Higgins taught

indicators.note: to polish is to work over and refine, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to a snooker player to buff the cue rather than oil it.
explanation.walkthrough: Higgins is both a snooker champion, which fits 'cue', and Professor Henry Higgins of Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, who coached Eliza Doolittle's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Higgins was a phonetics professor teaching correct pronunciation and clear speaking, which is elocution.

clue.text: Transport gin to bar

indicators.note: to transport is to move things, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Carrying gin over to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, such as gold.

clue.text: Bloody unusual

definitions.meaning: of steak, lightly cooked so still red and bloody inside

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise: how odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare steak is underdone and bloody, and rare also means seldom seen.

clue.text: Detective describes short story one finds appealing on the box

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the detective goes around the rest

parts.note: TEC is short for detective

indicators.note: short says the last letter of the story word is lopped off

parts.note: a legend is a story
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A TV detective tells a brief story that someone finds charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the story word; 'describes' wraps the detective around it and I. The box is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone telegenic looks attractive on television.
